Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
656 AM EDT Mon Aug 31 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 223 AM EDT Monday...

Forecast for broader rains Monday evening into Tuesday continues to 
trend southwards.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 223 AM EDT Monday...

1. Dry today, and light shower activity possible on Tuesday.

2. A vigorous low will be capable of producing locally heavy 
rain and thunderstorms on Wednesday into Wednesday night.

3. Trending drier into the weekend with a few chances for 
lingering showers as an upper low departs to the east.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 223 AM EDT Monday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Widespread fog across Vermont and northern New York will 
give way to supremely comfortable weather today. Patchy mid to high 
level clouds will continue to stream along sluggish boundary to our 
southwest. So the Northeast Kingdom should be nice and sunny, while 
the North Country sees a bit more cloud cover. Temperatures will 
rise into the 70s during the afternoon with light winds.

For this evening and overnight, the range of high res and global 
models remain in better consensus of a southward position of 
elevated convection along the aforementioned quasi-stationary front. 
The high res guidance the last several days likely had some 
convective feedback, and now that we're closer, those models have 
less time to get carried away. There should still be a swath of 
moderate rain along the borderlines with our neighboring forecast 
offices across Vermont and northern New York and little to no rain 
across far northern Vermont. This also lowers the likelihood of 
thunder. Pulled QPF back even further from the previous forecast. 
About a third to half inch is likely in southern Rutland/Windsor 
counties, and approaching the southern Adirondacks and far souther 
St. Lawrence Counties, and just a couple hundredths at Vermont's 
international border. During the evening and overnight, a trough 
will begin to develop while surface pressures rise along Coastal New 
England. This appears like it will trap moisture along eastern 
slopes. If forecast soundings weren't too dry near the surface, I 
would think this would be a drizzle/mist type set up. Flow aloft 
remains somewhat fast, so perhaps there some forcing that produces 
very light rain showers that linger into Tuesday night.

KEY MESSAGE 2: The more potent system appears to be the Wednesday 
system. A trough tracking across the Northern Plains will eject east 
as it gets caught between a closed upper low north of the Great 
Lakes and an upper high in the southeastern US. Favorable conditions 
for height falls will allow the development of a strengthening 
surface low across the Great Lakes quickly moving east by Wednesday 
afternoon. Initially, we'll still have high pressure in the Canadian 
Maritimes holding dry stable air east and west-northwest flow aloft 
still maintaining the line between this dry air and warm, moist air 
to our south. As the surface low develops a warm front will shift 
east late morning into the early afternoon. Light rain should push 
west to east, but any rain from it will be tempered by the low-level 
dry air. That warm front will shift just north of the international 
border, and then the surface low will follow Wednesday night. 
Increasing instability (mostly aloft) and sharp frontogenetic 
forcing against stubborn high pressure will produce thunderstorms 
that will be capable of heavy rainfall. The degree of elevated 
instability remains in question, and there will almost certainly 
still be some wobbles in the exact track as we've seen for Tuesday's 
system depending on convective processes and where exactly low 
pressure will track along a still present sluggish thermal/moisture 
gradient.

KEY MESSAGE 3: Our Wed/Thu system will occlude Thursday night off the 
southeast New England Coast, dragging its parent low southeast with 
it. Showers look to continue as wrap around moisture lingers across 
Vermont, with some drying in northern New York. The upper low will 
drift over northern Maine by Friday keeping cyclonic flow 
northeasterly flow entrenched. While most of the late week and 
weekend looks to be on the drier side, isolated to scattered 
diurnally driven showers during the day will be possible, mainly 
over eastern Vermont and the Adirondacks. Current precipitation 
chances are around 35-50%, with the exception of the higher terrain 
which currently have PoPs to 60-70%. Any daytime shower activity 
will wane by the evenings. Skies look to remain on the cloudy side 
Friday into Saturday. Friday looks to be the best chances for rain 
in the late week and weekend with rain chances decrease each day 
towards next week. Temperatures will generally be seasonable in the 
60s and 70s, but there is a chance for some lower temperatures than 
current guidance is suggesting across eastern Vermont should more 
clouds, and precipitation develop. Overnight lows will trend cooler 
into the weekend towards the mid 40s to low 50s as subtle ridging 
and some radiational cooling nights are to be expected heading into 
next week.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
Through 12Z Tuesday...Fog has developed at all terminals this
morning. Conditions look to improve back towards VFR between
12-13Z for BTV/PBG/RUT, and closer to 13-14Z for EFK/SLK/MPV.
MSS will trend towards MVFR by 13Z with low stratus around 
1500ft agl, ten VFR by 14Z. Quiet VFR aviation conditions are 
expected after 14Z through 00Z with mainly clear skies, and 
light and variable terrain driven winds. Clouds back build in 
after 00Z tonight with showers possible at all sites except EFK 
beginning after 00Z through the end of this TAF period.

Outlook...

Tuesday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Likely SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.
Tuesday Night: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Wednesday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Likely SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.
Wednesday Night: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance
SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Thursday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Thursday Night: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance
SHRA.
Friday: MVFR/IFR conditions possible. Chance SHRA, Slight chance
TSRA.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
